title: Collision & Trigger Events
description: Write code that reacts when objects touch – OnCollisionEnter, OnTriggerEnter, and their friends.

slides.title: Detecting Physical Hits 💥
slides.content:
# Collision Messages

When two non-trigger colliders make contact, Unity sends messages to all scripts on both objects. You can implement these methods to react:

- `OnCollisionEnter(Collision collision)` – called when contact begins.
- `OnCollisionStay(Collision collision)` – called every physics step while contact persists.
- `OnCollisionExit(Collision collision)` – called when contact ends.

The `Collision` object holds info about the impact (relative velocity, contacts, impulse, gameObject).

quizData.question: What parameter type does OnCollisionEnter receive?
quizData.explanation: OnCollisionEnter receives a Collision object with detailed impact data.

slides.title: Trigger Events 🟢
slides.content:
# Entering Without Touching

If a collider has `Is Trigger = true`, you get different messages:

- `OnTriggerEnter(Collider other)` – when another collider enters the trigger zone.
- `OnTriggerStay(Collider other)` – every physics step while inside.
- `OnTriggerExit(Collider other)` – when it leaves.

The `Collider` parameter gives you access to the other object and its gameObject.

Use these for pickups, checkpoints, and sensor zones.

quizData.question: Which method is called when a Rigidbody enters a trigger collider?
quizData.explanation: OnTriggerEnter is called for trigger interactions.

slides.title: Required Conditions ⚠️
slides.content:
# For Messages to Fire

- At least one object must have a **Rigidbody** (or Rigidbody2D).
- For collision messages, neither collider should be a trigger.
- For trigger messages, at least one must be a trigger.
- The layers of the objects must be set to interact in the **Physics Collision Matrix** (Edit → Project Settings → Physics → Layer Collision Matrix).

If events aren't firing, check these settings.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use CompareTag, Not ==

Always check tags with `other.CompareTag("Player")` instead of `other.tag == "Player"`. CompareTag is faster and allocates less memory.
